newsitem.title: USA: NYS Dorm Auth sets 16 bond sales totaling $378 mln.
newsitem.headline: NYS Dorm Auth sets 16 bond sales totaling $378 mln.

text.p: The New York State Dormitory Authority on Friday said that from April to June it planned 16 bond sales for colleges and medical centers that add up to almost $378 million.
A breakdown of the negotiated offerings, which the Authority cautioned was subject to change, follows:
--Menorah Campus, about $39 million during the week of April 7, underwritten by Cain Bros.
--Hebrew Home of Riverdale, about $12 million during the week of April 14, underwritten by Samuel A. Ramirez & Co.
--Siena College, about $30 million during the week of April 15, underwritten by Morgan Stanley.
--Metropolitan Eye, Ear and Throat Hospital, about $20 million, underwritten by PaineWebber.
--New York University, about $20 million during the week of April 28, underwritten by Morgan Stanley.
--Beth Israel Medical Center, about $30 million during the week of April 28, underwritten by Goldman Sachs.
--Teresian House, about $22 million during the week of April 28, underwritten by First Albany Corp.
--Lakeside-Beikirch Nursing Home, about $12 million, underwritten by Cain Bros.
--Champlain Valley Physicians Hospital Medical Center Community Providers Inc, about $29 million during the week of May 5, underwritten by Merrill Lynch.
--Millard Fillmore Hospitals Inc., about $96 million during the week of May 5, underwritten by Merrill Lynch.
--Arden Hill Life Care Center/Wesley Health Care Center, about $16.9 million during the week of May 12, underwritten by Smith Barney.
--Winthrop University Hospital, about $10 million during the week of May 12, underwritten by J.P. Morgan Securities.
--St. Mary's Hospital, about $11 million during the week of May 26, underwritten by First Albany Corp.
--CAMBIA Primary Care, about $5 million during the week of June 2, underwritten by J.P. Morgan Securities.
--Eger Nursing Home, $13 million during the week of June 2, underwritten by Cain Bros.
--Center for the Developmental Disabled/Children's Home of Kingston, about $12 million during the week of June 16, underwritten by First Albany Corp.
